summary.headline: Greenlam Q4 FY26 consol revenue rose 26% YoY to INR858 crore, with EBITDA pre-forex up 57% to INR107 crore; FY26 PAT fell 18% to INR56 crore.
summary.overview: FY26 consolidated revenue crossed INR3,000 crore, up 18.6% to INR3,046 crore, with EBITDA before forex up 21% to INR334 crore. Q4 was the strongest quarter, with revenue of INR858 crore and EBITDA margin before forex of 12.5%. Full-year PAT fell 18% to INR56 crore, which management attributed to chipboard operating losses plus higher interest and depreciation in the first full year of the chipboard plant. Management guided to about 18% top-line growth in FY27 and no new capacity beyond two laminate lines in Andhra Pradesh, with the focus on utilising existing assets.

financial_highlights.change: Company expects to reduce by about INR50 crore in FY27

financial_highlights.value: 51 days in Q4; 57 days for FY26
financial_highlights.change: Q4 improved 4 days from 55 days; FY26 level broadly flat

segments.name: Laminates & Allied
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR658 crore (+14% YoY), EBITDA margin before forex 17.2% (+350 bps); FY26 revenue INR2,433 crore (+9.3%), margin 15.9%. Q4 sales volume 5.15 million sheets (+4.5%) at INR1,243/sheet; FY26 utilisation 86%.

segments.name: Plywood & Allied
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR119 crore (+18% YoY), EBITDA loss before forex INR3.8 crore; FY26 revenue INR400 crore (+18.4%), EBITDA loss INR29.5 crore. FY26 realisation INR257/sq m; Q4 INR246/sq m. Utilisation about 45-50% in Q4.

segments.name: Panel & Allied (Chipboard)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR80 crore (+47% QoQ), EBITDA loss before forex INR2.2 crore, utilisation 49% and sales volume 38,800 cubic metres (+34% QoQ) at INR20,562/cubic metre. FY26 revenue INR213 crore, EBITDA loss INR23 crore, utilisation 39%, realisation INR19,370/cubic metre.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top-line growth of about 18%, maintained despite raw material cost pressure and possible demand disruption.
Laminates revenue growth of about 10-12% in FY27.
Plywood and chipboard expected to reach EBITDA breakeven in FY27; chipboard breakeven stated as achievable around 50% utilisation.
Two new laminate lines at Andhra Pradesh expected to start production by end of FY27, adding about 2 million sheets of capacity; management sees no need for a fifth plant.
No new capacity additions beyond the two laminate lines in FY27; plywood pan-India expansion not expected until FY28.
Plywood realisation expected to stay flat or move only a few percentage points; no significant upside seen.
capex_capacity: Two laminate lines being added at Andhra Pradesh plant, about 2 million sheets, expected by end of FY27; brownfield, so faster than greenfield.
Laminate capacity: management says about 20% headroom at 86% FY26 utilisation; laminate utilisation has reached 108-110% annualised in the past.
Chipboard plant (first year of operation) is stabilised; utilisation 39% for FY26 and 49% in Q4, targeted to rise further.
Plywood utilisation about 45-50% in Q4; management aims for near-full utilisation of existing plant by FY28.
Pre-laminated chipboard share is rising; management ambition is up to nearly 100% of chipboard output laminated; share not disclosed on call.
demand_pricing: Price increases were implemented from April 2026 after raw material costs rose from March due to the West Asia conflict; most RM cost increases passed on domestically, and 4-5% in export markets plus rupee depreciation.
Some softening in chemical raw material costs since; minor market price corrections.
No demand destruction seen so far, but secondary sales are weak and cash flows tight in the market; some customers postponing projects and some stocking up earlier.
Middle East exports impacted in March and April; May normalised. Management says impact is limited.

Competition: larger organised players gaining share from midsized and unorganised players under cost and cash-flow pressure; closest domestic competitor is of similar size. Internationally competes with Wilsonart, Formica and regional players.
Plywood Q3 weakness was due to certification issues, resolved in Q4, with good March sales.

qa_highlights.question: What laminate growth is expected in FY27 and is the company outpacing the industry?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects laminate top-line growth of about 10-12% in FY27 and believes it may be outpacing the industry, though it cannot verify industry data. Distribution, product range and presence in domestic and international markets are cited as drivers.

qa_highlights.question: Plywood realisation outlook as the business matures?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said realisation may stay broadly flat, with changes of only a few percentage points, because it is already near the top of the category price range. Growth will come from volume, including the lower end of premium categories. Tier 2 is not being targeted.

qa_highlights.question: Peak laminate utilisation and need for further expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said utilisation has reached 108-110% annualised in the past and could get there again depending on mix. With two million sheets of capacity due by year-end and about 20% headroom at 86%, no further expansion is needed for now, and the position is reviewed quarterly.

qa_highlights.question: Margin outlook and breakeven timing for plywood and chipboard?
qa_highlights.answer: Laminate margin is expected at about 16-17%. Plywood and chipboard are both expected to break even in FY27; chipboard Q4 loss narrowed to about INR2 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Reports of particle board plants converting to MDF?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not aware of any such conversions. It believes the processes differ and that particle board demand will grow with the QCO for furniture.

qa_highlights.question: Demand impact of the war-driven price increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said demand has held for the last two months, but secondary sales are weak and some projects are delayed. Supply disruption from smaller players helped the company. It sees mixed signals and a possible slowdown if prices stay high.

risks_watch: Raw material costs (chemicals) and their pass-through; Q4 gross margin fell 410 bps QoQ on input costs.
West Asia conflict: Middle East export disruption in March-April, freight and transit delays.
Weak secondary sales and tight customer cash flows could slow demand.
Chipboard and plywood breakeven in FY27 is a key test; FY26 losses pushed PAT down.
Rising interest and depreciation from new capacity; net debt of INR940 crore, with only about INR50 crore reduction planned.
Laminate Andhra Pradesh lines due by end FY27; execution risk.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the core laminates business and on FY27 growth targets, but cautious on demand visibility and raw material costs. Management was evasive on the share of pre-laminated chipboard sales, deferring it to an offline discussion.
key_quotes: And FY27 will be one more year where we're not getting new capacities on board.
So realization in the ply business may not go up in any significant manner.
We've seen that in Europe also and many other markets, chipboard gradually over the period of time has become one of the largest substrate or panel product.
So clearly, we see this as an opportunity more than a crisis.

adds.what: 2 laminate lines at Andhra Pradesh plant (~2 million sheets capacity), brownfield

growth.why: Management maintains ~18% FY27 consolidated top-line growth (laminates 10-12%), backed by two brownfield Andhra Pradesh laminate lines (~2 million sheets, due by end FY27), 86% laminate utilisation with ~20% headroom, and plywood/chipboard ramp; no specific order book figures were given, so backing is partial.
